ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg AML/CFT legal framework: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 February 2019; Law of 19 December 2022 implementing the ECJ judgment of 22 November 2022 (Case C-37/20) and restricting public UBO access; CSSF Regulation 12-02 (AML/CFT) and CSSF Circulars on PEP/EDD; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Articles 23, 26-29); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS); Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions (autorisation d'établissement).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (restricted access): full UBO data accessible to Luxembourg competent authorities (FIU Cellule de Renseignement Financier, CSSF, Autorité d'État, notaries, credit institutions and tax administration); access to financial-sector professionals and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; no general public access since the Law of 19 December 2022.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) incorporating the approved Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary admitted to practice in the Grand Duchy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization - no apostille or consular legalization required for the deed itself; mandatory registration with the RCS within 30 days of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate confirming the blocking/deposit of the EUR 12,000 minimum share capital (attestation de consignation de capital)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution holding the blocked account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic bank certification issued in the name of the future SARL; no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / registry excerpt (extrait du registre) of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial or companies registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Convention of 5 October 1961) if the source state is a Contracting Party; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Luxembourg embassy or consulate with territorial competence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract (extrait du casier judiciaire) for each proposed gérant (manager) of the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Ministry of Justice (Parquet général) or the competent judicial authority of the manager's state of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic issuance by Luxembourg authorities, or Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization when issued abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of valid national ID cards or passports of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and each gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original issuing authority of the respective state or a notary public competent to certify copies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized or legalized certified copies; for non-EU/EEA documents, supplemental Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of the underlying identity document where the destination institution so requires

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Business plan with three-year financial projections and preliminary AML/CFT internal control note
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders and the M&A advisory boutique's management, prepared with Luxembourg local counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No public authentication required; submitted to the bank, the RCS/RBE for substance review, and to the Ministry of the Economy when applying for the autorisation d'établissement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening per the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004, CSSF Regulation 12-02 and FATF Recommendation 12: (1) positive-name-match screening against the consolidated EU restrictive measures/terrorism sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions (1267/1988, 1373), OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury sanctions and the Luxembourg domestic list of persons linked to terrorist acts (Arrêté of 30 October 2008, as amended); (2) PEP identification covering both foreign and domestic PEPs and their family members and close associates per Directive (EU) 2018/843 and CSSF guidance; (3) enhanced due diligence (EDD) with source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification for PEPs and high-risk third-country clients; (4) electronic screening audit trail retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship; (5) ongoing transaction monitoring and escalation protocols to the Luxembourg FIU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL): https://www.lbr.lu / https://www.rcsl.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the primary statutory filing language of the RCS. The corporate name must be rendered in Latin characters and may contain French, Luxembourgish, German, English or other words provided they are written in Latin script and are unambiguous. Non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin alphabet in the RCS filing. The name must contain a distinct denominative element and the mandatory legal form marker 'société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. The name must not mislead as to the company's object or legal form, must not contravene public policy, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or earlier Benelux trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS objection or refusal of the proposed name (normally notified within five working days after filing), the applicant or its notary may (1) immediately submit alternative candidate names through the LBR portal without additional filing fee; (2) if the objection rests on a substantive legal or trademark ground, file a formal appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) by petition filed through a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour within one month of the refusal notification, per the procedure of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS; (3) where the Tribunal rejects the name, appeal to the Cour d'appel within 40 days of the judgment; (4) simultaneously, conduct a Benelux Office for Intellectual Property (BOIP) trademark search and, if necessary, file a trademark opposition. A name refusal does not block the incorporation process; the notarial deed may be executed under a substituted name and the original name position re-filed as a trade name (nom commercial) where permissible.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted and not recommended for this activity. A Luxembourg SARL must maintain a registered office (siège statutaire) in Luxembourg. For an M&A advisory boutique carrying a Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML rating and requiring a statutory business authorisation, the Ministry of the Economy, the FIU and the CSSF expect genuine economic substance: physical office premises accessible during business hours, retention of books and records, AML/CFT files, and effective day-to-day management exercised in Luxembourg. A pure 'virtual office' (mail-forwarding address without staff or record retention) is not compliant. A serviced-office or administrative agent may support compliance administration but cannot replace the operational seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-High - approximately 35-40% annualized probability of an unannounced physical inspection. The FIU, the Ministry of the Economy and the RBE supervisory authority each hold inspection powers under Article 36 of the AML Law of 12 November 2004, the Law of 2 September 2011 and the Law of 13 January 2019; cross-border deal-flow activity in the medium-risk tier increases the exposure to on-site substance verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff - no charge for name availability search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation UBO piercing and sanctions screening audit file (EU consolidated list, UN Security Council, OFAC SDN, domestic Luxembourg lists and PEP database checks for all founders, gérants and UBOs)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for enhanced Stage-1 due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the Articles of Association (statuts), share transfer pre-emption clauses and consular legalization coordination
Notarization of the Acte constitutif (notarial scale fee including registration formalities and disbursements)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial scale tariff (tarif des notaires) plus out-of-pocket expenses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration fee and publication of the incorporation extract in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
Mandatory RBE beneficial owner declaration filing post-incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff - filing free of charge; mandatory within one month of incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment licence) application for the M&A advisory activity under the Law of 2 September 2011
Hague Apostilles and/or consular legalization fees for two to three foreign corporate and identity documents (shareholder registry extracts, identity documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs / Luxembourg diplomatic or consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per apostille or consular legalization (varies by issuing state)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening, KYC onboarding of signatories and issuance of the capital blocking certificate (attestation de consignation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark account setup and administration charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial share capital deposit - EUR 12,000 equivalent placed in a blocked account as statutory minimum capital requirement (released to the SARL upon RCS registration; not a state charge)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital requirement under the Law of 10 August 1915; refundable deposit held by the company

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Articles 100 to 158 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended and consolidated (SARL regime); Articles 1 to 8 and 33 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2011 on RCS filings
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), with mandatory electronic filing through a Luxembourg civil-law notary
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) incorporating the full Articles of Association (Statuts), filed electronically with the RCS and followed by legal publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued share capital: EUR 12,000. The capital must be fully subscribed; at least 25% of each cash share must be paid up on incorporation and deposited in a blocked pre-incorporation bank account with a Luxembourg credit institution, evidenced by a bank blocked-funds certificate (attestation de consignation) addressed to the notary. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up at signing and specifically described in the deed. No escrow agent is required beyond the notary's control over the blocked account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscriptions for the entire issued capital of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée are hereby confirmed and accepted, and that the paid-up portion evidenced by the bank's blocked-funds certificate is approved. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the address specified in the notarial deed, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the Manager is authorized to lease such premises and register the Company with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole signatory power and full powers to open bank accounts and file VAT and tax returns. RESOLVED, that directorships are declined and the Manager shall indemnify the Company per the Articles of Association.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Pre-Incorporation Capital Blocking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary and a Luxembourg credit institution (pre-incorporation bank account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to perform an availability search in the RCS name index and reserve the proposed corporate name. Open a pre-incorporation bank account with a Luxembourg credit institution and deposit at least 25% of the subscribed share capital (EUR 12,000 minimum) in blocked funds, or the full capital in the case of in-kind contributions. Obtain a blocked-funds certificate (attestation de consignation) from the bank and deliver it to the notary together with the draft articles of association drafted in French or German.
required_dossiers: Name availability confirmation from RCS index search
Draft articles of association (statuts)
Valid passport or national ID of each shareholder and proposed manager
Bank blocked-funds certificate (attestation de consignation)
Proof of residential address of each signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit two or three alternative names for reservation within the RCS procedures; if the bank declines the pre-incorporation account, transfer funds to another credit institution and re-obtain the blocked-funds certificate without restarting name clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholders and the proposed manager must appear before the notary, or be validly represented by proxy, to sign the deed of incorporation and the articles of association. The notary verifies the identity of the signatories, the full subscription of capital, the adequacy of the blocked-funds certificate, and the statutory mandatory content under Articles 100-158 of the Law of 10 August 1915. The original notarial deed is signed and held as an authentic act, and certified copies are prepared for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Final draft deed of incorporation and articles of association
Bank blocked-funds certificate
Valid ID documents of all shareholders and manager
Power of attorney for any absent shareholder
Declaration of non-conviction and good standing of proposed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Material defects are cured by executing a corrective notarial instrument before the same or another notary within 15 days; minor drafting errors may be corrected through a rectification deed without re-executing the shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Registration with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), submitting via the notary's secure electronic channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary uploads the signed deed of incorporation and the RCS registration form through the official LBR portal, attaching a certified electronic copy of the notarial deed and paying the state filing fee. Upon admission, the RCS allocates the company's 14-digit RCS registration number, registers the manager, and issues an RCS extract; the legal entity identifier is subsequently obtained through the entity registration process.
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation (certified electronic copy)
RCS registration form completed and certified by the notary
Statutory extract listing name, registered office, capital, and managers
Proof of payment of the RCS filing fee
Consent declarations of the appointed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a completion notice requesting supplementary information, the notary cures the deficiency within 15 calendar days by refiling the corrected documents; a refusal of admission may be appealed to the Tribunal de Commerce within two months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Publication in the RESA Electronic Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS admission, the notary submits the legal publication extract to the RESA bulletin within one month of the deed. The published notice contains the corporate name, RCS number, registered office, share capital, and managerial appointments. Publication in RESA is a condition for the effectiveness against third parties of the deed and certain statutory particulars.
required_dossiers: RCS registration confirmation with allocated registration number
Publication extract signed by the notary
Payment confirmation of the RESA publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is deferred or the extract contains inaccuracies, apply to the RCS/LBR editor for rectification; if the editor refuses, a rectification order can be sought from the Tribunal de Commerce within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Security, and Business Establishment Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Ministry of Economy - Master of Trade (Maître de Métier)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after incorporation, register the company for Luxembourg VAT (TVA) using the RCS extract and Article 104 legal entity form; register the Manager and any employees with CCSS for social security; file the pre-declaration with ITM where employees are hired; and apply for the autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) through the Guichet des entreprises portal for the M&A advisory office activity.
required_dossiers: Certified RCS extract
Certified copy of the articles of association
Legal entity tax registration form (formulaire 104)
Proof of registered office (lease agreement or ownership title)
Valid ID and criminal-record extract of the Manager from country of origin
Employment status and social security declarations for any staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies may be regularised within one month by voluntary submission of missing documents; refusals of the establishment permit can be appealed to the Minister of Economy and thereafter to the Administrative Tribunal; late registrations attract administrative fines and interest, which may be mitigated through voluntary disclosure before formal notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy - Direction générale du développement économique, acting through the Master of Trade (Maître de Métier) and the Guichet des entreprises e-commerce portal; premises-level permits issued by the competent communal authority in Luxembourg City or the registered-office commune
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for non-regulated professional advisory and consulting services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category A non-industrial office activity: no full EIA or EIA registration is required for a professional services boutique absent industrial installations, fuel-burning equipment above thresholds, or premises classified as a classified installation (établissement classé); only an optional simplified environmental registration applies if the leased office exceeds 500 m² gross floor area or the fit-out generates construction waste above the regulatory threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater and no significant VOC emissions expected; office sanitary discharge must comply with municipal sewer by-laws (BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, COD ≤ 1,000 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 350 mg/L at connection point); office waste must be source-sorted and removed by carriers registered with CELTIS; heating and cooling installations must meet the energy-performance thresholds of the Law of 4 August 2021; any future fit-out works must respect the construction waste management protocol of the Administration de l'environnement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for the leased office premises, including accessible exits, alarm systems, and extinguisher placement; structural load and electrical safety certificate from an approved bureau de contrôle (e.g., Secolux, APAVE, DNV) confirming floor load capacity and electrical conformity; occupational health and safety registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); mandatory employee health-surveillance contract with a licensed occupational health service (Service de Santé au Travail) when staff are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), www.acd.public.lu. Indirect taxes: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), VAT Department, https://aedt.public.lu. Single digital entry point: www.guichet.lu / www.myguichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the SARL with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) within 15 days of formation; the RCS national registration number is the statutory general TIN under Luxembourg law. 2) File VAT registration Form 645 (Demande d'immatriculation TVA) with the AEDT via myGuichet.lu prior to commencing taxable activity; the AEDT issues a VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits). 3) Registration is compulsory when expected annual taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000, and may be voluntary below this threshold; non-resident companies operating a Luxembourg branch or fixed establishment use the same Form 645 and must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative if established outside the EU. 4) Foreign entities claiming treaty relief or fiscal regimes must attach a certificate of fiscal domicile issued by their home tax authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (opaque capital company; the Luxembourg SARL is a societe de capitaux, not eligible for pass-through; subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and the solidarity surcharge on worldwide profits for resident companies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid classification election exists under Luxembourg law. Available elections: 1) Tax consolidation (fiscal unity) under Art. 164bis LIR for qualifying 95% Luxembourg/EU/Norwegian/Icelandic subsidiaries, binding for at least five fiscal years; 2) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Art. 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for financially, economically and organizationally integrated persons; 3) Small-business exemption waiver (Art. 57a VAT Law), permitting the taxable person to opt into normal VAT liability below EUR 35,000; 4) Participation exemption election per Art. 166 LIR for qualifying dividend and capital-gain relief subject to holding-period and substance conditions. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are automatically neutralized under ATAD 2 (Arts. 168a-168f LIR), and DAC6 disclosure obligations apply to reportable cross-border arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutee - TVA), governed by Directive 2006/112/EC as transposed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small-enterprise exemption, Art. 57a VAT Law). Mandatory registration for a Luxembourg-established supplier once turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed this threshold; non-established suppliers must register for the supply of goods in Luxembourg without threshold (intra-Community distance sales exceeding EUR 10,000 may use the EU OSS regime instead of local registration).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime is in force as of 2025. Mandatory B2B e-invoicing with structured formats (EN 16931) and VAT digital reporting to the AEDT via the national OsiLo platform is announced with effect from 1 January 2026. E-invoicing via the PEPPOL network has been obligatory for suppliers to Luxembourg public entities since 18 April 2019. Until the B2B mandate becomes effective, paper or PDF invoices remain valid provided they satisfy the Fields of Arts. 57-60 VAT Law (sequential numbering, VAT ID, date, supply description, and tax amount). The M&A boutique must issue compliant VAT invoices for all Luxembourg-taxable fees; success fees and fixed fees charged under reverse-charge arrangements require a clear mention that VAT is shifted to the recipient.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies to exports of goods to non-EU destinations (Art. 54 VAT Law) and to intra-Community supplies when the EU customer has a valid VAT ID validated in VIES (Art. 53 VAT Law), subject to EC Sales List and recapitulative statement filing. Services: cross-border B2B advisory services, including M&A success fees, are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the place-of-supply rule (Art. 57 VAT Law) because the services are deemed rendered where the business customer is established; hence no Luxembourg VAT is charged and the foreign recipient accounts for reverse charge or local VAT. The 0% rate may also apply to services directly connected with exported goods (Art. 54(1) VAT Law). Zero-rating or non-application claims must be evidenced by written contracts, engagement letters, customer VAT identification and payment flows.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD / IE515 via Luxembourg LUCAS single window) or Intrastat declaration (DEB) for intra-Community dispatches
Transport evidence of physical departure: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note (or warehouse certificate for customs-warehoused goods)
Commercial invoice and M&A advisory engagement letter / success-fee agreement evidencing the nature, place and beneficiary of the services
Proof of payment and foreign-exchange repatriation: SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit advice or bank statement confirming receipt from the foreign client within 180 days
Validation of customer B2B status: VIES-valid EU VAT ID for intra-Community services/supplies, or certificate of foreign tax residence for extra-EU service recipients
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VAT reassessment periods are three years ordinarily, extended to five years for transactions giving rise to cross-border supplies or information exchange with foreign competent authorities, and ten years for VAT fraud (fraude fiscale) under the Abgabenordnung. Unwarranted zero-rating is clawed back with monthly interest of 0.60% (7.2% p.a.) from the due date. Administrative fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years for aggravated fraudulent conduct, imposed under the VAT Enforcement Law of 1 December 2009; directors and the beneficial client may be held jointly and severally liable. The AEDT conducts focused audits on advisory boutiques claiming service export treatment, scrutinizing economic substance, board-managed documentation, and actual performance versus invoice narrative; failure to substantiate the non-resident customer and value of consideration triggers immediate reassessment and penalty exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg operates under the Eurosystem single-currency framework, with no separate foreign-exchange control authority. Resident banks carry statutory responsibility for BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting and CSSF AML/CFT supervision under the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility under Eurozone membership and EU free movement of capital (TFEU Article 63; Directive 88/361/EEC). Current-account flows, including success fees, advisor commissions, and cross-border reimbursements, and capital-account flows, including equity injections, shareholder loans, and deal-escrow settlements, are unrestricted for residents and non-residents. Profit-repatriation hurdles are purely fiscal: domestic dividend withholding tax is 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when a 10% shareholding is held for 12 months, or under most double-tax treaties to 5% or less; no central-bank clearance, foreign-exchange permit, or repatriation license is required. One prudential limit applies: a non-bank SARL may not accept deposits or intermediate client deal monies outside a credit-institution escrow structure, by reason of Article 2-1 of the Law of 5 April 1993.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to remit export receipts or cross-border advisory success-fee proceeds to the central bank. Receipts may be retained in EUR or any freely convertible currency (USD, CHF, GBP) and may be reinvested offshore without restriction. The sole compliance duty is statistical: resident banks attach BCL balance-of-payments purpose codes to each inbound and outbound wire for macro-financial data collection, with no exchange-control effect.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR account; segregated escrow sub-ledger available for M&A deal-milestone monies under a professional escrow annex

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for the SARL's own operating funds; Low for client and deal funds. A PSD2-licensed electronic-money institution (Luxembourg-authorised or EU/EEA-passported, such as Airwallex, Payoneer, or a Luxembourg e-money issuer) can hold the boutique's own balance, execute SWIFT and SEPA/instant transfers, and issue virtual IBANs settled through TARGET2. Legal constraint: under the Luxembourg Law of 1 April 2019 implementing PSD2 safeguarding rules, an EMI may not hold M&A client monies or third-party escrow funds in the manner of a credit institution. Client success-fee collections and deal escrows must settle at a licensed credit institution; therefore the EMI is a viable secondary rail for own-account professional fees and expenses only, never the primary treasury anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De jure, Luxembourg AML/CFT law permits remote onboarding via eIDAS-qualified electronic identification, videoconference interviews, and notarially certified copies. De facto, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks will not onboard a Medium-Risk-Enhanced advisory boutique without at least one in-person meeting of the authorized signatory or Ultimate Beneficial Owner at the bank's premises or before a Luxembourg notary, supported by original or notarially certified passports, proof of residence, and the RBE beneficial-ownership excerpt. Where the UBO resides outside the EU/EEA, most banks require a physical interview plus a banker's reference from the UBO's home regulated institution. Remote opening is accepted only when the application is chaperoned by a Luxembourg-licensed notary or accountant with active RBE registration and a pre-existing bank relationship; otherwise an in-person milestone is effectively compulsory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or authorized signatory resident in a FATF grey-listed or high-risk jurisdiction, or with any nexus to sanctioned states
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and residence permits; Luxembourg RBE beneficial-ownership excerpt; source-of-wealth statement with chain-of-title for all contributed assets; three years of personal tax returns; FATF-compliant sanctions-screening output; independent professional reference from an EU-regulated attorney or accountant; source-of-funds affidavit expressly mapping the capital-injection route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border success-fee wires from Cayman, BVI, Delaware SPVs, or offshore acquisition vehicles inconsistent with the announced M&A advisory mandate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed engagement letters; executed purchase or securities-purchase agreements with deal timelines; success-fee waterfall clause; bank statement trail for the identified deal; closing confirmation from target counsel; escrow instruction chain; commercial-registry extracts of each SPV client; explanatory memorandum linking each wire to a named mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perception of unlicensed deposit-taking when the account receives third-party deal funds for onward distribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion under Article 2-1 of the Law of 5 April 1993 confirming absence of deposit-taking; executed escrow agreement appointing the credit institution as escrow agent; client-money-flow chart proving pass-through with zero-day holding; signed undertaking that no interest accrues to the SARL; independent auditor's AML-controls comfort letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Front-loaded liquidity, namely large inbound equity or shareholder-loan deposits before completed M&A engagements, creating bank-fraud and laundering typologies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially acknowledged share-capital-increase deed or shareholder-loan agreement with repayment schedule; audited capital-adequacy evidence; 12-month treasury plan; M&A mandate pipeline table; contractual evidence of committed deal targets with projected close dates; board resolutions authorizing the funding; Luxembourg corporate-tax number and RCS excerpt.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for a SARL: (1) equity injection, where the investor wires via SWIFT MT103 from its own account to the SARL's EUR IBAN, with the bank instructed to classify the transfer as BCL balance-of-payments code for equity capital; the wire must be accompanied by a notarised increase-of-capital deed or contemporaneous shareholder resolution and UBO passport; (2) shareholder loan, coded as intercompany loan, non-resident, with an executed loan agreement, arm's-length interest indication, and repayment schedule; (3) third-party deposits are blocked. No BCL or CSSF prior clearance applies to EU/EEA or OECD-origin inbound capital, but the bank independently verifies source of funds and ultimate beneficial ownership; any inbound wire lacking the underlying corporate deed is held in suspense pending documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfer via TARGET2, carrying full structured remittance information and the deal reference to pass bank sanctions and OFAC screening. For EUR payments below EUR 100,000, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) is the efficient second rail; for USD, GBP, and CHF beneficiaries, MT103 with nostro routing is used. Acquisition deposits and deal-closing circuits may be supported by commercial letters of credit under ICC UCP 600 or bank demand guarantees and bid bonds issued on the SARL's pledged collateral, although M&A advisory fee settlements are normally pure MT103 wires rather than documentary collections. Disbursement policy must align each wire's purpose to the invoiced mandate, and the bank retains the audit record for AML defence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright vanilla FX forwards with maturities up to 24 months under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with a Luxembourg credit institution
FX swaps for short-dated treasury rebalancing of USD, CHF, and GBP success-fee receipts
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for long-dated fee receivables and earn-out alignment
Plain-vanilla FX options restricted to hedging purposes, requiring MiFID II professional-client classification and a CSSF-compliant suitability assessment

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible only for genuine underlying exposure to restricted-convertibility currencies such as CNH, INR, or BRL, and not market-standard for EUR/USD/CHF/GBD; an onshore-leg hedge or natural multi-currency mirroring is preferred
Multi-currency account grid (EUR/USD/CHF/GBP) used as a zero-cost structural hedge to avoid forced conversions on large inbound success fees

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 201 (Déclaration pour l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l’impôt commercial communal et l’impôt sur la fortune) — filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu/E-TAX portal (eCDF XML declaration).
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: For a SARL on a calendar year (FY ending 31 Dec), the return must reach the AED (Administration des contributions directes) by 31 December of the immediately following tax year; legally, within 3 months after the tax return form is officially served, and no later than the 31-December statutory backstop; extensions may be requested via the e-TAX portal before the backstop.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS number (Luxembourg Trade Register), national identification number (N° national), seat address, legal form (SARL), and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the local fiscal representative's name for non-resident directors; the SARL itself is always a Luxembourg resident taxpayer if its central administration or registered office is in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting year; status as a resident (résident) company, full liability to CIT/MBT/NWT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident managers do not alter tax residence; Luxembourg-resident status follows from the SARL's registered seat or place of effective management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal activity code: ISIC 7020 (Management consultancy activities) / NAICS 523150 (Investment banking and securities dealing – M&A advisory); description: cross-border M&A boutique.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the EU NACE code fully aligned to ISIC 7020 - not the personal non-resident taxpayer code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory balance-sheet totals (share capital, retained earnings, shareholder loans, intercompany receivables/payables, cash).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where shareholder loans from foreign shareholders exist, attach a table showing interest rates applied and the functional currency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit before tax per the annual accounts; must reconcile to the statutory accounts approved by the shareholders' general meeting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile any US-GAAP/IFRS adjustments to Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) before entering the figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disallowed expenses: corporate income tax itself, municipal business tax, non-deductible entertainment costs >20% of documented business meals? (Luxembourg: 50% of restaurant costs non-deductible?), interest paid on excessive shareholder debt, fines, contributions to non-compliant pension plans.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, any hidden profit distribution (e.g., salary payments without adequate substance to a foreign manager) must be added back automatically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income/capital gains; IP box deduction (80%); notional interest deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach proof of 12-month holding period and ≥10% participation (or €1.2M acquisition cost) for any foreign dividend relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Taxable result and set-off of carried-forward losses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (revenu imposable) after loss relief; loss history table with yearly set-offs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners cannot use Luxembourg losses in their home country; state the settled loss carry-forward figure used.
